comparison: Perfect agreement on morphological classification (C21-C44). Both recognize the quality and validity of the descriptive findings identifying 10 distinct arbor types with detailed quantitative measurements. OpenEval emphasizes the extensive quantitative data supporting the classification, while peer reviewers acknowledge the quality of results and morphometric assays.

Complete agreement on single-target innervation findings (C26-C28). Both accept the observational data showing 20/20 MCA arbors isolated at P21, with appropriate caveats about axon breakage and developmental timing. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Agreement on uncertainty regarding directional sensing (C33, C61-C63). Both accept the morphological observations about orientation and positioning but consider the functional interpretation speculative. OpenEval notes lack of physiological validation; peer reviewers flag this as speculation that may dilute the paper.

Disagreement on coverage factor estimates (C65-C71). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to assumptions underlying calculations and need for validation. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting these as part of the morphometric quantitative assays without raising specific concerns about the methodology.

Complete agreement on experimental advantages and future prospects (C79-C87). Both recognize the technical advantages of the cutaneous system and the methodological contributions. The optimistic projection about future comprehensive description is accepted as appropriately qualified speculation.

Agreement on uncertainty for receptive field predictions (C55-C60, C64). Both evaluations recognize these as reasonable but unvalidated predictions requiring physiological confirmation. OpenEval emphasizes need for electrophysiological mapping; peer reviewers note these represent speculation about function that remains to be seen.

Agreement on uncertainty for morphology-function correlations (C49-C54). Both recognize these proposals as reasonable but speculative without direct validation. OpenEval notes appropriate qualifying language but lack of experimental confirmation; peer reviewers observe more morphologies than known functions and question correspondence to function.

Strong agreement on morphological uniformity findings (C45-C48). Both recognize this as a significant original contribution. OpenEval supports the inference about functional uniformity; peer reviewers explicitly state this is 'the best support for the validity of the classification method' and note it was difficult to appreciate from prior studies.

Agreement on uncertainty for developmental competition model (C72-C74, C78). Both recognize these as speculative hypotheses requiring experimental validation. OpenEval notes C73 has citation support but broader model is speculative; peer reviewers flag these as speculation that may dilute the paper.

Disagreement on follicle polarization claims (C75-C77). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to speculative polarity transmission mechanism (C78 included in R14). Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, accepting the quantitative observation (C75) and established anatomical facts (C76-C77) without challenge.

Agreement on experimental design and tissue processing (C8-C13 overlap). Both accept the methodological approach with specific quantitative details. OpenEval validates tissue preservation measurements; peer reviewers acknowledge quality of results and morphometric assays, noting sampling limitations are not impediments to publication.

Disagreement on Brn3a hemizygosity (C5-C7). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on transcript compensation evidence and functional equivalence. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting this is 'not fully discussed' and requesting more explicit acknowledgment of potential subtle phenotypes despite accepting compensatory autoregulation as strongest counterargument.

Agreement on genetic labeling strategy (C1-C4 overlap). Both recognize the intersectional genetic approach as valid and having general implications. OpenEval validates expression patterns and allele structure; peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge the method without critique of design or implementation.

Complete agreement on sampling limitations (C19-C20). Both accept the authors' frank acknowledgment of incomplete sampling and size-dependent bias. OpenEval notes appropriate scientific caution; peer reviewers explicitly state these limitations are not impediments to publication and are fully understood by authors.

Agreement on labeling approach limitations (C16-C18). Both accept the logical inference about intersection of expression domains and enrichment in large-diameter neurons. These limitations are acknowledged as appropriate caveats without challenging the validity of the approach.

Agreement on reproducibility validation (C91-C92 overlap). Both accept the technical precision demonstrated by reproducibility assessment showing 2.17% and 5.60% differences. Peer reviewers acknowledge this supports the morphometric quantitative assays developed by the authors.

Agreement on tissue clearing validation (C88-C90 overlap). Both accept the tissue processing measurements demonstrating preservation of tissue dimensions. These methodological details are not challenged and support the validity of the quantitative approach.

Agreement on sample sizes (C14-C15 overlap). Both accept the reported sample sizes (719 arbors surveyed, 77 fully traced) as providing adequate statistical power. Peer reviewers acknowledge the methodological approach without raising concerns about sample adequacy.

Agreement on uncertainty for LD-FALE functional role (C64 overlap). Both recognize this as a logical but unvalidated hypothesis about function based on morphology. OpenEval requires physiological and behavioral validation; peer reviewers flag as speculation about function that remains to be seen.

Agreement on uncertainty for polarity transmission mechanism (C78 overlap). Both recognize this as speculative despite unpublished observations mentioned by authors. OpenEval notes hypothesis is unvalidated without presented data; peer reviewers flag as speculation that may dilute the paper.

Disagreement on labeled-line model conclusion (C49 overlap). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, stating the conclusion logically follows from morphological diversity and within-type uniformity (though notes physiological validation would strengthen). Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether morphological classification corresponds well to function given more morphologies than known functions.
